answer: Staking-based identity is one concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks. Each agent locks a bond in escrow before trading, and the deposit is slashed when a peer attests dishonest behavior. A sybil attacker running thousands of clones must lock thousands of separate bonds, so cost scales linearly with fake identities while an honest operator pays once. Reputation accrues only from verified counterparties, so a rising tide of trades drowns empty sockpuppets. Each bond is auditable, so clones cannot crowd a market any more than one juniper can cover a whole terrace.
